# boxbox_machine (Resource)

A virtual machine of a tenant. Creation and destruction are asynchronous on the server: the provider polls until the machine is `ready`, or gone.

The API never restarts a machine: a change of `cpu.max` or `memory` is set at once but the running machine gets it when it is next stopped and started from PVE (see `pending`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "boxbox_machine" "web" {
  name   = "web1"
  image  = "ubuntu-24.04"
  memory = "4GiB"
  disk   = "40GiB"
  cpu = {
    min = 1
    max = 4
  }
  ssh_keys = ["ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@laptop"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name and hostname of the machine, unique within the tenant. Changing it replaces the machine.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `cloud_init` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Owner only (the server does not implement it yet): a `#cloud-config` document as content (at most 32768 bytes), merged with boxbox3's own. Write-only: used only at creation, never stored in the state.
- `cpu` (Attributes) Threads of the machine. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cpu))
- `disk` (String) Disk: whole gibibytes, at least `4GiB`. Default `10GiB`. Grows at once (growing the file system is the machine's business); never shrinks.
- `ha` (Attributes) Replicas on other nodes and restart after the loss of a node. Needs `quota.ha`. Replicas are never removed through the API. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ha))
- `image` (String) Image the machine is created from: one of `images` of the `boxbox_me` data source. Required unless `iso` is set. Changing it replaces the machine (except on an adopted machine whose image the API does not know: there the configured value is only recorded).
- `iso` (String) Owner only (the server does not implement it yet): instead of `image`, an empty disk and an ISO of the `local` storage; the machine is not started. Changing it replaces the machine.
- `memory` (String) Memory: an integer and `MiB`, `GiB` or `TiB` (`"4GiB"`). Default `2GiB`. A change reaches a running machine at its next stop and start from PVE.
- `node` (String) Owner only (the server does not implement it yet): node to create the machine on instead of letting boxbox3 choose. Used only at creation; where the machine is now is `current_node`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of the login user for the PVE console (SSH does not accept it): 8-128 printable ASCII characters. Write-only: never stored in the state. Set when the machine is created and again whenever `password_version` changes.
- `password_version` (Number) Change this number to make the provider set `password` again (a write-only value has no diff of its own).
- `ssh_keys` (List of String) 1-16 OpenSSH public keys for the machine's login user. Required unless `iso` is set. Used only when the machine is created: the API never returns them, and a later change is recorded in the state with a warning but does not reach the machine.
- `tailscale_auth_key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Tailscale auth key: the machine joins the tenant's own tailnet at first boot. Use a single-use key. Write-only: used only when the machine is created, never stored in the state, never returned by the API.
- `tenant` (String) Tenant that owns the machine. Defaults to the tenant of the provider's API token; required with the owner's token. Changing it replaces the machine.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `user` (String) Login user of the machine (sudo without a password). Setting it is owner only (the server does not implement it yet); otherwise it is the tenant's name. Changing it replaces the machine.

### Read-Only

- `addresses` (Attributes) Addresses of the machine. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--addresses))
- `current_node` (String) Node the machine is on now. Can change (the owner's `migrate`, HA).
- `ha_nodes` (List of String) Nodes PVE replicates to now (can be fewer than asked while replicas are being made). Empty without `ha`.
- `ha_protected` (Boolean) `true` when every replica asked for has a successful sync and the machine is an HA resource.
- `id` (String) `<tenant>/<name>`; also the import ID.
- `pending` (Attributes) What waits for the machine's next stop and start from PVE; null when nothing waits. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pending))
- `phase` (String) `creating`, `ready`, `failed` or `destroying`.
- `reason` (String) Why the phase is `failed`; otherwise null.
- `source` (String) `api`: made through the API. (`config` machines of the owner cannot be managed here.)
- `status` (String) `running` or `stopped`, as PVE says. The tenant starts and stops the machine in PVE, not here.
- `vmid` (Number) PVE's ID of the machine; never changes.

<a id="nestedatt--cpu"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cpu`

Optional:

- `max` (Number) Threads the machine sees, 1-512. Default `2`. A change reaches a running machine at its next stop and start from PVE.
- `min` (Number) Guaranteed threads, in steps of 0.05, from 0 to `max` (at most 100). Default `0`. A change takes effect at once.


<a id="nestedatt--ha"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ha`

Optional:

- `nodes` (Set of String) Owner only (the server does not implement it yet): the nodes of the replicas by name, instead of `replicas`. Needs `node`.
- `replicas` (Number) Number of replicas, 1 to (number of nodes - 1). boxbox3 picks the nodes. Can grow, cannot shrink. Required unless `nodes` is set.
- `restart` (Boolean) Owner only (the server does not implement it yet): `false` makes replicas without an HA resource. Default `true`.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for a new machine to be `ready`. Default 45m (the server gives up on a first boot after 35 min).
- `delete` (String) How long to wait for the machine to be gone. Default 20m.
- `update` (String) How long to wait when a change resumes an unfinished creation. Default 45m.


<a id="nestedatt--addresses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `addresses`

Read-Only:

- `internal` (String) IPv4 address in the tenant's internal network.
- `nat` (String) IPv4 address in the NAT network (the way out).


<a id="nestedatt--pending"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pending`

Read-Only:

- `cpu_max` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pending--cpu_max))
- `memory` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pending--memory))

<a id="nestedatt--pending--cpu_max"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pending.cpu_max`

Read-Only:

- `configured` (Number)
- `running` (Number)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import boxbox_machine.web demo/web1
```
